title: adaptive-heap-slab-allocator-and-spill-coalescer-for-kv-cache
author: Ravi Patel
description:
Context: the existing KV cache allocator mixes slab buckets and general-purpose allocations which leads to fragmentation under mixed small/large KV shapes. Frequent small spills (many tiny files/objects) were observed on high-concurrency continuous-batching workloads, causing IO amplification and pressure on the spillback storage tier. Motivation: reduce memory fragmentation, reduce the number of small spill writes, and make eviction decisions less disruptive to in-flight continuous batches. Summary: this PR introduces an adaptive heap-slab allocator and a spill coalescer component: 1) adaptive heap-slab allocator: a hybrid allocator that keeps a small number of size-classed slabs for hot, small entries and a contiguous "heap region" for larger / variable-sized entries. The allocator tracks fragmentation metrics per arena and can promote/demote arenas between slab and heap modes at runtime based on usage patterns. 2) spill coalescer: a background writer that merges multiple small spill candidates into sequential, sized spill objects to reduce IO ops and improve write throughput to object storage. 3) eviction policy change: eviction now prefers demoting entries from slab arenas first and defers eviction of entries predicted to be rereferenced soon (short reuse-distance) using a lightweight LRU sketch. 4) scheduling hints to kernel selection: we propagate a small hint from the KV layer so the serving runtime can pick more compact kernels that favor lower memory footprint when cache utilization is high. 5) continuous-batching coordination: the cache exposes an opt-in fence API so ongoing batches can pin prefixes to avoid being evicted mid-query; the allocator avoids reclaiming pinned memory and will instead trigger spill/coalesce earlier. Checklist: - [x] design doc: docs/design/kv-adaptive-heapslab-and-spill.md (internal) - [x] unit tests for allocator and demotion/promotion paths - [x] integration test for coalesced spill behavior under high QPS - [x] microbenchmarks showing memory / IO improvements - [x] feature flag gated rollout (env VAR: KV_HEAP_SLAB_ENABLE)

Implementation notes: - New modules: server/kv/heap_slab_allocator.rs, server/kv/spill_coalescer.cpp, server/kv/eviction_policy.rs, serve/runtime/kernel_hints.h. - Heapslab allocator keeps per-NUMA arenas with a small slab footprint (configurable: slab_target_pct) and uses a fast freelist for slab allocations. When slab fragmentation exceeds a threshold (frag_pct) the arena will do an async compaction pass to consolidate or will demote to heap mode if compaction would be costlier. - Spill coalescer batches spill candidates within a time window (coalesce_ms, default 8ms) or when the aggregate size reaches a threshold (coalesce_bytes, default 256KB). Spills are written as sequential objects named by sequence id to the configured spill backend. - Eviction policy: a two-stage heuristic: prefer slab-dominated arenas for eviction, then fall back to heap region. Entries pinned by batch_fence are exempt; the policy records eviction rejections and increases coalesce aggressiveness when rejections spike.

Test plan and results: - Unit tests added: allocator invariants, promotion/demotion, compaction correctness. - Integration: kv-spill-e2e run against S3-compatible local backends: reduced number of spill objects by 28% on a mixed small+large synthetic workload. - Perf: end-to-end serving benchmark (continuous batching, 16 concurrent clients, seq_len=512): 95th percentile tail latency improved by 12% (from 210ms to 185ms) under heavy cache pressure; median CPU on GPU host decreased ~6% due to fewer small IO wakeups; steady-state memory fragmentation metric (measured as free_small_chunks / total_free) improved from 0.42 to 0.18. - Safety: feature behind ENV flag and rollout plan; default disabled for Dedicated clusters until validated.

Migration and rollout: - Feature flag rollout: disabled by default. - Canary on internal perf clusters for 2 weeks, then opt-in for selected customers. - Telemetry added: kv.alloc.mode, kv.frag_pct, kv.spill.coalesce_rate, kv.eviction.rejections.

Known limitations: - Worst-case demotion path can cause transient CPU spikes during async compaction; added backoff heuristics but further tuning may be necessary. - Coalescer currently targets object store backends and is not yet tuned for file-system-backed spill in on-prem bundles.

Related work: ENG-4123 (allocator fragmentation study), ENG-4178 (spill IO reduction spike). Design doc: internal link: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-4123/kv-adaptive-heapslab-and-spill-coalescer. Merge notes: squash-merged to main, feature gated. If regressions occur, revert by toggling KV_HEAP_SLAB_ENABLE or rolling back the commit.

review_comments: Maya Chen (2026-02-15): Requested change: the demotion path needs a stronger backoff to avoid CPU spikes during compaction. Also please add histogram buckets for kv.spill.size.
Ravi Patel (2026-02-16): Reply: added exponential backoff and histogram buckets; updated tests to assert backoff behavior.
Elena García (2026-02-18): Approved after small nits: rename coalesce_ms -> coalesce_window_ms, and add documentation for the fence API semantics.
Thomas Nguyen (2026-02-21): Left an optimization suggestion: consider combining slab freelists across low-traffic arenas to reduce fragmentation; opened a follow-up ticket ENG-4210.
Maya Chen (2026-02-25): Final approval after CI green and bench numbers validated on perf cluster.
release_notes: Improves KV cache memory utilization and reduces small-spill IO: introduces an adaptive heap-slab allocator, spill coalescing, and a revised eviction policy. Feature gated via KV_HEAP_SLAB_ENABLE. Expected benefits: lower tail latency under heavy cache pressure, fewer small spill objects, and reduced memory fragmentation.
